ideas.title: Set the brushes for the load: Lumi's hand on the rocker while the motor hauls
ideas.critique: This answers both of round 1's worries. L and flux are tabulated from saturating solves over angle and both currents, contact resistance comes from patch overlap, the spark energy is whatever is left in the coil, and Lumi's hand really turns the rocker. Its weak point is that it leans on the winch existing: without the real rope load the moving optimum falls back to a bench motor with a typed load, and the 'faint violet' spark has to be an emitter driven by that 1/2 L i^2, not a tinted sprite.

ideas.title: The winch: hook anything, it hauls or stalls
ideas.critique: Round 1's fitted speeds are gone: a rod-chain rope with IPC wrap, a cart whose mass comes from mesh volume and which rolls by contact, and torque from the circuit each step make this general. Hooking anything and picking a pulley is a real choice the physics decides. A cart creeping on planks is slow to watch, and a rod chain wrapping a drum under IPC with a motor torque fed in is where it will break or quietly get swapped for a spring.

ideas.title: Wind the coil with your own hands
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This fixes round 1's 'scales with N': the field solve takes the conductors where the rod actually lies, the resistance comes from its length, and the unbalance becomes a bearing force, so how you wind is what the motor is. Laying dozens of turns by hand risks being tedious, and the Ferrite mesh rebuilt from rod positions in each slot is the hard part that could shrink into a bunching coefficient.

ideas.title: Fit the bearings: it binds or it runs
ideas.critique: Friction that comes from the contact normal force of misalignment is the honest way to do it, and 'works only when the parts fit' is exactly the human's direction. But shimming an axle until it spins is a fiddly upkeep task with one target state, and IPC contact on sliver shims at bearing tolerances will either jitter or need tuning until the answer is typed in.

ideas.title: The cart's oak frame takes the friends' weight
ideas.critique: Anisotropic oak FEM with pegs that fail in shear gives building a structure with real stakes, and its mass carrying into the winch load ties it into the machine. The predictable part is the payoff: friends climb on and it sags or splits, which is a reaction shot. The choice of thickness and bracing only matters if the frame really feeds the load later.

ideas.title: A compass needle that reads the current
ideas.critique: A tangent galvanometer from the em.jl field of the real turns plus the island's field is sound physics, but on film it is another needle swinging on its own, close to the compass bowl. It only becomes a gauge worth having once there is something worth measuring, so on its own it is a technique waiting for a use.
